why: The Shelf is merged into the Journal (display only; the flag stays in storage): '/shelf' predates that, and every old link, bookmark and 'Send to the Shelf' door still resolves by redirecting to the Journal. The Shelf's own system board is still derived and still a board, and a harness mounts it: '/shelf-board' is the old bridge unchanged in shape (find-or-create, idempotent, no router state). No chrome links to it.

A device that signed out goes to sign-in and stays there: every route except the door itself and the guest link (its token rides in the hash) goes back to '/', after the boot check, so a signed-in device is never bounced. BrandMark below is one logo, a faint bottom-right watermark, absent at '/' (Arrival mounts its own).

installed once for the whole session (App.tsx mounts regardless of route or auth state), not tied to SyncIndicator's own mount, which renders in more than one place; see beforeUnloadGuard.ts for the reasoning and the Electron exclusion

the router mounts regardless of auth state: Arrival (route '/') is both the boot screen and the front door; Write works local-first with no account, and the Journal, Drawers and Projects all run on local data, so only startSync() above is authed-only. Arrival's own boot bar (authState as a prop) carries the loading state.

The splash, mounted at the app root rather than on a route: it belongs to every app OPENING, not to '/'. It renders once per load, is pointer-events:none throughout, and dims whatever is mounted behind it (Arrival at boot). `ready` is Arrival's own boot-bar derivation (authState !== 'loading'), so the splash holds longer while the app is not ready.
the unborn surface, declared BEFORE /page/:id so the literal segment wins the match; a blank-surface door lands here with its descriptor in the query string and creates no row

The guided-path CONTENT: for every step of every Tier 1 deck, the QUESTION a dealt card carries as its placeholder (q), the one plain "?" sentence (e) and one example (x), parsed by a script from the deck-content doc (md5 347e3efc057eece588c27dc28d1d5c3a), never retyped. A sibling file, not deskLexicon's CANONICAL: this is deck content, not chrome, so no theme overrides it and the sentences stay out of the lexicon census. Every word lives in this one file, reached only through stepQuestion / stepExplain / stepExample. Where a question varies by the deal's own answer, `q` is a record keyed by the answer's option id. Examples are for the "?" only: never on a card, and never sent with a Tutor ask unless the writer opened that entry.

The deck engine's pure heart: turns a deck's declared card set (DealtCardSpec[], local `key`s only) into a real Box[] (generated ids, real 'connection' threads) without touching persistence. Zero schema: a dealt card has the same shape as a hand-typed "Add card" box and owes its template nothing, except that a guided step (a Tier 1 deck's dealt card) carries ONE pointer, `deckStep: { deck, step }`, and its question as `prompt`, both optional, written only here on a NEW deal. `spec.title`/`spec.body` arrive already resolved through deskTerm() (see decks/types.ts's DealtCardSpec). Threads dedupe either direction (as BoardEditor's finishThreadDrag does), so two cards naming each other mint ONE connection. Callers own the one mutation, always the ordinary boxes-array path (saveBoardBoxes for a new board; plain setBoxes on the Board, riding its debounced autosave, since a separate saveBoardBoxes there would race the unflushed in-memory boxes).

The deck library in Machina's dress: two pieces of DATA the panel needs, both read from the real registry. blockRangeLabel(deck) is a row's block count: a RANGE where the deal question changes it (Three-Act 6-9, Argumentative Essay 5-7), one number where it does not (Story Circle 8), nothing for a deck that deals a block per page the writer picks (From my pages); computed from the deck's own deal() over every combination of its choice questions, so it cannot drift. FORMS_GROUPS is Machina's seven group labels, each with its decks; the registry's rooms map onto them (a group's `room` is its decks' room; the label is the lexicon's), and every registered deck appears exactly once. The one hand-set figure: Character Study reads "2-4 x" (two to four characters, a count the writer chooses).

"Help me choose" (the librarian / RUN DIAGNOSTIC / Intake / Scout), the logic only: three questions, the pick table, Q3's landing. Pure data and functions, no React, storage, randomness or model: the same answers give the same result in every theme (the questions are deck content, not chrome). Nothing is stored, and nothing here opens a panel (components/HelpMeChoose.tsx opens only on a press). The census harness (scripts/harness/help-choose-census.mjs) checks this module row by row against an independent transcription of the table and against the deck registry. A CHOICE is a deck plus the deck's own deal answers when the table names one; {} means the deck asks its own question when dealt. "Fifteen Beats (Feature, with the Pilot note)" is the deck's own pilot option.

Q3's landing. A little: the pick deals and opens in the Walk with the first step's "?" already open. The shape: the Walk, "?" closed. Everything: Open (the table), all cards at once, no Walk. With the Walk not shipped (the switch false), all three open as Open. Nothing is stored.

Character Study, dealt PRE-THREADED: each character gets the same four self cards (want vs. need, the wound, the contradiction, voice notes), with composed titles ("<Label> <letter>: <type title>", both halves through deskTerm(), the letter generated); each ADJACENT pair of characters gets one Relationship card, threaded to both sides' Want vs. Need card. The wizard offers two, three or four characters: one would carry no relationship card, so the deal would not be pre-threaded.
a card's title carries no font marks

FROM MY PAGES, the reverse outline: look at what you already wrote and name what each part is doing. The writer PICKS pages, in their order (the wizard's `kind: 'pages'` question, components/DeckWizard.tsx); the deck deals ONE CARD PER PAGE, in that order, each titled with its page's title (or first words) and GRAFTED to that page (`graftTo`; the caller grafts it through the board, decks/engine.ts MaterializedDeal.grafts). It only shows: nothing here writes, reorders or moves a page (the only store import is a READ, getJournalEntry), and a card's graft is the ordinary Grafts record a writer could make by hand. The card's body is empty, its question "What does this part do for the whole?"; the Gaps readout is not a card and is not dealt. Answers: `pages` = the chosen entry ids joined by ',' (in the order picked); a deal with none deals nothing, and the wizard never offers it.

the ship set: the six flagships plus Character Study, the threads demonstration. This array is the ONE place the set lives; every door (CreateProject.tsx, BoardEditor.tsx) reads it, never a hand-copied list.

Thesis / Dissertation, the Academy's flagship. Wizard: humanities / sciences. Five foundation cards always deal (research question, lit-review clusters, methodology, evidence parking lot, citation list); the sciences branch swaps the four generic chapter cards for IMRaD chapter shapes: the same card count (9) either way, a different chapter SET, not just different prompts.
each card is a question (decks/guided.ts, decks/content.ts): [title, step id]. The humanities chapter titles stay Chapter One / Two / Three.

The deck engine's shape. A Card Deck is a preset: an optional wizard that narrows choices, then deals a pre-built set of cards onto a board. This file is the ENTIRE static-data contract a deck definition satisfies; the engine (DeckWizard.tsx + engine.ts) is deck-agnostic: it renders what a definition declares and calls its own `deal`. Zero schema: a DeckDefinition is a plain static in-memory object, never persisted, never user data, shipped with the app like KIND_META/PICKER_GROUPS (store/kindLabels.ts); nothing here is a database row or a new Box field. Lexicon discipline: every string a definition names is a DeskTermId (a lexicon KEY), never a raw string, resolved through deskTerm() at deal time (engine.ts), the non-hook escape hatch persistence.ts's SYSTEM_BOARD_TITLE_TERM and kindLabels.ts already use.

The sheet's dimension: what a page IS as paper, as opposed to its face+size, which is its VOICE. One shape serves both the per-page value and the per-user default, because "set as my default" is a copy of the open page's settings; two shapes would drift. Below it, the page's declared kind and the style guide, as PLACEHOLDERS: they render and persist per page, and nothing downstream is wired yet; what isn't built doesn't render. NOT named `PageKind`: `DeskFrame.pageKind` already means which SURFACE renders ('prose' | 'screenplay' | 'board'); this is what the writer DECLARES the page to be. Zero schema: both keys ride `journal_entries.page_settings` jsonb as optional, absent-never-null members of PageSettings, so an untouched page is byte-identical and reads `undefined` -> the defaults here. No column, no migration, no backfill.

preselected: Normal is the page's kind until the writer says otherwise, and MLA is the style guide on Research's FIRST reveal. Read through `?? PAGE_KIND_DEFAULT`, never written at birth: writing them would dirty every page that never asked.

Proofing: the writer's dictionary, dialect and ignore blob. One nullable jsonb column, `users.proofing`, on `users.page_defaults`' recipe: per WRITER, not per page, so it is neither `pageSettings` nor a second tenant of `page_defaults` (that column is the starting DRESS; proofing is a different concept).
the default, changeable and never prompted for

A removed word's tombstone expires after this many days (compaction, not a cap). Named rather than inlined because the consequence is a behaviour a reader should be able to find: a device offline longer than this can bring a removed word back.

optional and ABSENT (never null) on every page that never chose, which keeps an older row byte-identical. Not in PAGE_SETTINGS_FALLBACK below: the fallback is the app's DRESS floor, and a page's kind is not its dress; readers default through PAGE_KIND_DEFAULT / STYLE_GUIDE_DEFAULT.
a TEXT card's own face and size (the options live in the card's tool strip; the default is the everyday font). Additive inside `boxes` (jsonb), zero schema, and ABSENT on every card that never chose.

A DEALT STEP IS A QUESTION, NOT TEXT. Two additive optional fields inside the board's `boxes` jsonb (zero schema: sync stores the blob whole, as with fontFace / seq / onCanvas), written ONLY by a NEW deal of a Tier 1 deck: prompt - the step's question, resolved at deal time (store/guided.ts, decks/content.ts). The card's PLACEHOLDER, shown while it has no body, never in `text`, so it is never exported, copied, counted, synced as body or read by the Tutor as the writer's words (harness guided-w3 pins that no reader names `.prompt`). A written card keeps the field and stops showing it; delete the words and the question returns. deckStep - which step of which deck this card was dealt as ({ deck: 'three-act', step: 'hook' }): the key the "?" reads its sentence and example by, and what the Walk and coverage read. The card owes the deck nothing else.

The writer marks a step FINISHED by hand. One additive optional field inside the board's `boxes` jsonb (zero schema: sync stores the blob whole, like seq / onCanvas / deckStep). `true` = lit; ABSENT = not lit (unmarking REMOVES the key, so there is one way to be unlit), unmarked from the same door. A statement of the writer's, never a measurement: it never counts toward coverage (kindled() ignores it), never completes a Deck and never celebrates (store/guided.ts withLit, store/deckRewards.ts).

The writer sized this card by hand. One additive optional field inside the board's `boxes` jsonb (zero schema: sync stores the blob whole, like lit / seq / deckStep). `true` = hand-sized, the card KEEPS its size; ABSENT = auto, the card fits its content (grows and, once the writer has acted on it, shrinks). Set ONLY by a resize the writer performs on a text card; resizing back to its content height CLEARS it (the key is removed, so there is one way to be auto). Never set by a deal, a move, an edit or the reflow.

MEMBERSHIP IS NOT DISPLAY. A 'page-pin' Box is the membership record; the card on the canvas is one display of it. This flag gates the canvas and nothing else: `getBoardsPinning` reads membership by the pin's PRESENCE and never consults it, so a withheld card is still a member of the board everywhere. ABSENCE MEANS DISPLAYED: boards arranged before this field read `undefined` as "on the canvas" (no backfill, no migration); only an explicit `false` withholds. New memberships write `false` explicitly (pinPageToBoard), since a position is the writer's act. The `footerOn` shape: an additive optional field inside the board's `boxes` jsonb; sync.ts maps the whole blob (`JSON.stringify(e.boxes ?? null)` / `r.boxes ?? undefined`) with no per-field enumeration, so it costs zero schema, migration or server change.

A DELETED CARD IS A TOMBSTONE, NOT A REMOVAL. Three additive optional fields inside the board's `boxes` jsonb (zero schema: sync stores the blob whole): deletedAt - stamped when the card is sent to Trash; the box stays in `boxes`, hidden from every reader (store/boxTombstones.ts: liveBoxes), listed on the Trash board; Restore clears it. updatedAt - the per-box CHANGE TIME. Set when a card is deleted or restored; absent on every card that predates it. It alone decides which side of a merge wins. purgedAt - a permanent delete from Trash replaces the box with `{ id, kind, purgedAt }` + zeros. Final: a stale save cannot resurrect it.

A COPY GETS ITS OWN FIELD. `sourceEntryId` means "this card MIRRORS that entry", and BoardEditor's double-click dispatch is built on it: a text card carrying it TRAVELS to its source instead of opening the edit popup. A copy is the opposite relationship, independent (edits do not follow), so reusing the mirror field would cost a copy the editing gesture. One field, one relationship: additive optional, the `onCanvas` pattern, zero schema (`Box` rides the board's `boxes` jsonb). Read for the lineage line only (text, no travel); the dispatch is untouched.

TWO TRUE KINDS, Board and Book, as two optional additive fields on this board-meta box inside the board's `boxes` jsonb (the systemKind precedent: zero schema, no column, no migration, no server change). NOT named `kind`: Box.kind is the box discriminator ('text' / 'ink' / 'page-pin' / 'connection' / 'board-meta'). boardKind - 'board' | 'book'. Absent = a Board. The Journal's kind is DERIVED from systemKind and never stored on it; no other Book exists yet. homeView - the view the board opens in until the writer has chosen one on this device (the device-local "last shown as", store/boardMode.ts, beats it). Absent = the kind's default: a Board opens in Open, a Book in Flip. A Deck is a Board whose homeView is 'walk'. A value the kind does not have is ignored (store/boardKind.ts homeViewOf). It syncs (the whole boxes blob; last write wins): store/boardKind.ts withHomeView stamps this box's `updatedAt`, so the newer write wins the box-level merge (mergeBoxLists) rather than a tie going to whichever side won the entry.

linking is NOT a new shape: a card-to-card link is the EXISTING 'connection' box (connA/connB, an olive hairline BENEATH card faces, deletable, jsonb-in-`boxes`). FragmentLink is the rhizome ancestor; 'connection' is its board-side descendant. Open's thread gesture IS linking: no field added here.

The Tutor's per-page conversation thread: one nullable jsonb column on `journal_entries` (`tutor`, additive only, no default, no CHECK, like `origin`/`script`), mapped both ways in sync.ts (rowToJournalEntry / upsertJournalEntries). It holds the writer<->Tutor exchange for THIS page and its read cursor, nothing else: lens results and nudges are DERIVED, recomputed on every approach, never stored (a page's jsonb holds authored or generated content, never a cache of a computation that can be re-run). null <-> undefined is a fixed point through every client mutation path (persistence.ts's getTutorThread/saveTutorThread) and both sync directions: a page with no thread is absent, never an empty {messages:[]}. `role` is 'writer' | 'tutor' only; the system prompt binding the Tutor to the ghostwriter rail lives server-side, per request, never stored. `lastRead?: { at, chars }` is the listener's cursor, how much of the page's text the Tutor has read: a fact about the conversation, not a lens result or a nudge. It is optional because a thread with no cursor yet means "read from the start", never "read nothing"; it advances ONLY via persistence.ts's advanceTutorCursor, ONLY on a successful reply, and ONLY on a thread that already exists, so a page that never talked to the Tutor gains no persisted tutor state.

The Screenplay Room's document (conformant per `docs/fragments-under-pages-canon.md` §3). One styled block per element; a Scene is the addressable unit (its heading and body elements are fragments OF the scene, but links and ports always point at the Scene, never an element). `dual`/`struck`/`number`/`omitted`/`beatId` are reserved, not built: present here, never written by the UI.
